text:
Both halves settled.

(a) REFUTED -- my review claim was wrong. sacct does have --array: SchedMD documents it as "Expand job arrays. Display all array tasks on separate lines instead of displaying groups of array tasks on single lines" (https://slurm.schedmd.com/sacct.html). That is exactly what the accounting contract needs, and the existing fixture provenance was accurate. No code change; docs/compatibility.md corrected to describe JobID + --array and to say why JobIDRaw is deliberately not requested.

(b) CONFIRMED. squeue --jobs exits non-zero with "slurm_load_jobs error: Invalid job id specified" once a job leaves the queue, which is the ordinary end of every job; SlurmCliScheduler mapped every non-zero exit to InvocationFailed, so the most common poll in the library ended as a transport-shaped failure and one terminal job failed an entire batched observe. observe now recognizes that one documented diagnostic, conservatively, mirroring the SSH exit-255 policy: jobs the response still described stay observations, the rest become NotFound, and any other non-zero exit stays InvocationFailed. An all-absent recognized response is a batch of NotFound rather than Empty, because that is a statement about those jobs rather than about the query.

Evidence: three new SlurmCliSchedulerSuite tests (all-absent, unrecognized failure stays InvocationFailed, mixed partial response keeps the queued job and marks the departed one absent). cli 30/30, full gate green.

Live-capture evidence is tracked separately as P6f.33a; docs/compatibility.md states plainly that this recognition is derived from documented behaviour rather than a site transcript.
